Document description: Ethics baseline policy covering expected behaviors, reporting, disciplinary actions, and training. Key for G1 business conduct disclosures.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS G1 business conduct policy disclosures; GRI ethics & integrity/anti-corruption context; BRSR ethics and governance disclosures
What to capture (kernels): Scope, topics covered, training/attestation, breach handling, investigation workflow, training completion, breaches/investigations metrics
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: ESRS-G1-1 is primarily narrative. Quantitative items in this doc (training %, breaches count) should be maintained with a stable taxonomy, consistent population definition, and prior-year comparatives where available (even if not explicitly required) to support auditability.

Document description: CSR spend and program reporting. Useful for community investment, stakeholder outcomes, and social value narratives.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS 2 SBM contextual info; ESRS S3 community impacts (if material); GRI community investment disclosures; BRSR community development disclosures
What to capture (kernels): CSR governance, project register, spend totals and allocation, beneficiaries, outcomes/impact metrics, M&E method
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Materiality-gated (S3). If CSR metrics are used in ESRS responses, keep geography/program disaggregation consistent and track prior-year comparatives for spend and beneficiary metrics.

Document description: D&I commitments and management approach. Supports workforce diversity metrics and equal opportunity disclosures.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS S1 (equal opportunity/diversity/pay gap) where material; GRI 405; BRSR workforce diversity KPIs
What to capture (kernels): Scope/dimensions tracked, governance, commitments, accommodation, training, workforce diversity datasets, leadership/board diversity, pay equity method + metrics
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Use ESRS-S1-9 for the exact required breakdowns for governance body and workforce. Maintain consistent category taxonomy (gender, employee category, region as applicable) and provide prior-year comparatives where required.

Document description: Consolidated sustainability disclosure report, often multi-framework. Must be decomposed into kernels for ESRS mapping and gap analysis.
Framework relevance (framework-level): BRSR, CDP, ESRS, GRI, IFRS S1, IFRS S2, TCFD
ESRS DP ID(s) (from Crossmap): ESRS-E1-6 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E1-6-afecac1af11f4606865eeba198fe2b2f?pvs=21), ESRS-E1-7 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E1-7-54fcc9acba1345dca555959f65a21f28?pvs=21), ESRS-E1-5 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E1-5-0167155efc7f416693a381d16d03dd5b?pvs=21), ESRS-E2-4 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E2-4-20ed811484684dfdb7f760f816c3f95a?pvs=21), ESRS-E3-4 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E3-4-08e84370035d4311b6dfbad3951fc7dc?pvs=21), ESRS-E5-4 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E5-4-2fa545de72594e9f92fc265b8ee29893?pvs=21), ESRS-E5-5 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E5-5-858f720f208648d6af6de96adc92679a?pvs=21), ESRS-S1-9 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-S1-9-adc2945bfa584fefa79434803b64d4cb?pvs=21), ESRS-S1-14 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-S1-14-f86dc87a17c1497bad2fb83969c69d9c?pvs=21)
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS 2 + topical ESRS (E1–E5, S1–S4, G1) pre-fill source; GRI index crosswalk; IFRS S1/S2 narrative + metrics; CDP questionnaire responses; BRSR principles + KPIs; TCFD pillars (Gov/Strategy/Risk/Metrics)
What to capture (kernels): Framework claims + versions, disclosure index, policies/actions/targets by topic, KPI tables with methods/boundaries, restatements, uncertainty, assurance scope
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Use Crossmap DP rows for the exact required breakdowns. At minimum: Energy (E1-5) requires source/type split and comparatives; GHG (E1-6) requires Scope 1/2/3 and comparatives; Water (E3-4) requires source and stressed-area split and comparatives; Waste (E5-5) requires hazardous/non-hazardous and treatment route where applicable; Resource inflows (E5-4) requires material categories; Diversity (S1-9) requires workforce + governance breakdowns; H&S (S1-14) requires employee vs non-employee distinctions and rate methodology.

Document description: Occupational health and safety policy and management approach; ties to incident registers and rate metrics.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS S1 (health & safety) where material; GRI 403; BRSR workforce H&S KPIs
What to capture (kernels): Scope, governance, standards, hazard/risk method, incident workflow, CAPA, training matrix, H&S KPI definitions + datasets
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Use ESRS-S1-14 for exact KPI definitions, required breakdowns (employee vs non-employee), and comparative period requirement. Keep denominator basis for rates consistent year-on-year.

Document description: Defines conflicts and the declaration, approval, and management workflow; supports business conduct controls disclosures.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS G1 conflicts of interest controls; GRI governance/ethics context; BRSR conflicts of interest controls disclosures
What to capture (kernels): Definitions, disclosure triggers, declaration frequency, approvals/remediation, COI register fields, COI metrics
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Supports ESRS-G1-1 controls narrative. If tracking COI metrics, keep consistent definition of declaration scope (who files), frequency, and outcomes; retain year-on-year comparatives for trend evidence.

Document description: Policy and process for prevention of sexual harassment and complaint handling. Supports workforce conduct, grievance, training, and remediation disclosures.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS S1 grievances/harassment (if S1 material); GRI grievance and workplace conduct disclosures; BRSR workforce grievance/harassment disclosures
What to capture (kernels): Scope/definitions, IC committee, channels, SLAs/workflow, non-retaliation, remediation, training requirements, case metrics
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Treat POSH case metrics as a subset of ESRS-S1-17 where harassment/discrimination incidents are in scope. Keep employee vs non-employee separation where applicable, consistent case outcome categories, and prior-year comparatives.

Document description: Umbrella environment management policy. Anchors environmental governance, compliance commitments, and scope; connects to E1–E5 datasets.
Framework relevance (framework-level): BRSR, CDP, ESRS, GRI, IFRS S2, TCFD
ESRS DP ID(s) (from Crossmap): ESRS-E1-5 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E1-5-0167155efc7f416693a381d16d03dd5b?pvs=21), ESRS-E1-6 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E1-6-afecac1af11f4606865eeba198fe2b2f?pvs=21), ESRS-E1-7 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E1-7-54fcc9acba1345dca555959f65a21f28?pvs=21), ESRS-E2-4 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E2-4-20ed811484684dfdb7f760f816c3f95a?pvs=21), ESRS-E3-4 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E3-4-08e84370035d4311b6dfbad3951fc7dc?pvs=21), ESRS-E5-4 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E5-4-2fa545de72594e9f92fc265b8ee29893?pvs=21), ESRS-E5-5 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E5-5-858f720f208648d6af6de96adc92679a?pvs=21)
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS MDR-P (E-topic policies) when material; ESRS E1–E5 governance/policy; GRI management approach; CDP governance/policy narratives; BRSR Principle 6 environment management; TCFD governance/strategy context
What to capture (kernels): Scope/boundary, compliance stance, topic coverage, governance owner, review cycle, escalation, KPI list governed, supplier expectations
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Policy itself is qualitative, but it governs quantitative packs. Use linked ESRS DPs for required disaggregation and comparatives. Ensure policy scope matches the reporting boundary used in the linked quantitative metrics.

Document description: Primary statutory reporting pack. Use as source of boundary, business model, governance, risks, and financial anchors that many ESRS disclosures must reconcile to.
Framework relevance (framework-level): BRSR, ESRS, GRI, IFRS S1, IFRS S2, TCFD
ESRS DP ID(s) (from Crossmap): ESRS-E1-9 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E1-9-e7dfc7b824524f9a827733dd9f5a0f4e?pvs=21), ESRS-E2-6 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E2-6-a4febf3eff204ac1a5f32dc419bc74a3?pvs=21), ESRS-E3-5 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E3-5-c5777fcf2bd148f9ae33c0759f591a4d?pvs=21), ESRS-E4-6 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E4-6-93997cfbc67649269e416392fb26c78e?pvs=21), ESRS-E5-6 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-E5-6-94d28fbf2acd444db341b08e1e757df9?pvs=21), ESRS-1-PAR-44 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-1-PAR-44-dd032aa4525e4b71b4edb46246862761?pvs=21), ESRS-1-PAR-46 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-1-PAR-46-81c451dbc7fd424995c1ec180724e892?pvs=21)
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS 2: SBM/GOV/BP; ESRS 1 connected info; GRI 2; IFRS S1/S2 governance/strategy/risk anchors; BRSR general disclosures; TCFD Governance/Strategy anchors
What to capture (kernels): Entity boundary, consolidation basis, period/comparatives, segments/geographies, revenue/CapEx/OpEx anchors, business model + value chain, governance + ERM, principal risks
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Financial anchors used across multiple ESRS disclosures. Use the Crossmap rows for each topical "anticipated financial effects" DP to confirm whether revenue, CapEx, OpEx, and segment splits are required, and align period/comparatives to the sustainability statement reporting period.

Document description: Information security and privacy policy; can become material depending on business model and stakeholder impacts; supports risk governance narratives.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS 2 risk management narrative inputs if cyber/privacy IROs are material; IFRS S1 risk & resilience narrative; BRSR governance and customer/privacy narratives (as applicable)
What to capture (kernels): Data classification, access controls, incident response, third-party IT risk, training, breach metrics
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Entity-specific and materiality-dependent. If cyber/privacy becomes a material IRO, define incident taxonomy, severity thresholds, and ensure comparatives and methodology notes are maintained.

Document description: Policy and controls to prevent child labour in operations and supply chain; supports value chain due diligence disclosures.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS S2 value-chain workers (if material) + ESRS 2 due diligence process narrative; GRI human rights/supply chain disclosures; BRSR value chain and child labour disclosures
What to capture (kernels): Scope ops+suppliers, age verification, supplier clauses/screening, audits/monitoring, remediation, audit findings metrics
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Supports supplier management and due diligence narratives. If tracking screening and audit metrics, keep segmentation (tier/geography/risk), severity taxonomy, remediation closure status, and comparatives consistent.

Document description: Workplace conduct policy defining hateful activity and controls; ties to incident tracking and remediation.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS S1 workplace conduct and incidents where material; BRSR workforce conduct narratives and incident reporting
What to capture (kernels): Definitions/scope, reporting/investigation, disciplinary actions, training, incident metrics
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: If workplace conduct incidents are disclosed, align metrics to ESRS-S1-17 with stable definitions, outcomes taxonomy, and comparatives. Maintain confidentiality thresholds and avoid disclosing identifiable information.

Document name: Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action (EO/AA) Policy Statement
Document description: Equal opportunity commitments and affirmative action posture; supports workforce equal treatment disclosures.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS S1 equal opportunity disclosures (if S1 material); GRI diversity/equal opportunity disclosures; BRSR workforce representation and equal opportunity narratives
What to capture (kernels): Commitments/scope, recruitment & promotion controls, accommodations, complaint linkage, EO/AA metrics
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Use ESRS-S1-9 for representation metrics (required breakdowns). If discrimination complaints are tracked, align to ESRS-S1-17. Maintain consistent group taxonomy and comparatives.

Document description: Anti-bribery and anti-corruption policy; supports G1 controls and incident disclosures.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS G1 corruption and bribery prevention + incidents; GRI 205 anti-corruption indicators; BRSR anti-corruption governance and incidents
What to capture (kernels): Prohibited conduct, gifts/approvals, third-party DD, training, incidents/outcomes, controls monitoring
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: ESRS-G1-3 is the narrative control requirement; ESRS-G1-4 is the quantitative incident disclosure. Keep a stable case taxonomy and outcome categories so year-on-year comparatives are meaningful.

Document description: AML and KYC controls policy (as applicable); supports business conduct control disclosures.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS G1 business conduct controls where applicable; GRI ethics context; BRSR governance controls and compliance
What to capture (kernels): Scope/obligations, KYC/screening process, third-party screening, training, monitoring metrics
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Supports ESRS-G1-1 (business conduct policy/culture) and related controls narratives. If tracking quantitative AML/KYC activity, keep scope and definitions stable and retain comparatives.

Document description: Human rights commitment and due diligence approach; ties to value chain expectations, grievance accessibility, and remediation disclosures.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS 2 due diligence process + material topical S1–S4 disclosures; GRI human rights and supplier disclosures; BRSR social principles + value chain
What to capture (kernels): Scope ops+VC, standards referenced, salient risks, due diligence steps, grievance access, training, DD metrics, supplier requirements
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Due diligence is anchored in ESRS 2 GOV-4; incidents/complaints where workforce impacts arise can align to ESRS-S1-17. Keep consistent findings taxonomy, remediation closure status, and comparatives.

Document description: Umbrella grievance handling policy across stakeholder groups; supports grievance mechanism disclosures in S1–S4 and due diligence narratives.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS due diligence and grievance mechanisms across S1–S4 (materiality-gated) + ESRS 2 process narrative; GRI grievance mechanisms; BRSR grievance mechanism and resolution KPIs
What to capture (kernels): Stakeholder coverage, channels/accessibility, SLAs/escalation, remedy/appeals, grievance metrics
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Where used for workforce grievances, align to ESRS-S1-17 with consistent categories, resolution status, and time-to-close definition. For other stakeholder groups, treat as materiality-gated and keep stakeholder-type disaggregation consistent. Maintain comparatives for counts and resolution performance.

Document description: Speak-up / whistleblowing mechanism and investigation workflow; supports grievance mechanism disclosures and ethics incident metrics.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS G1 grievance/speak-up mechanism + case metrics; ESRS S1 grievance mechanisms where workforce-related; GRI grievance and ethics disclosures; BRSR whistleblowing mechanism and cases
What to capture (kernels): Channels/anonymity, non-retaliation, workflow/owner, hotline provider, taxonomy, case metrics
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Supports due diligence and business conduct narratives. If reporting case metrics, maintain a stable case taxonomy, stakeholder group mapping, confidentiality thresholds, and year-on-year comparatives.

Document description: Defines CSR governance, thematic focus, implementation model, partner management, and monitoring approach.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS 2 SBM contextual info; ESRS S3 community impacts (if material); GRI community investment disclosures; BRSR CSR / social contribution disclosures
What to capture (kernels): CSR governance/approvals, focus areas, partner DD, spend controls, M&E approach, project/spend datasets, impact metrics
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Materiality-gated (S3). If used for ESRS, maintain consistent definitions for spend allocation, beneficiary counting, and outcome KPIs. Provide comparatives where available.

Document description: Control environment for sustainability data and reporting. Critical for assurance readiness and ESRS 2 GOV-5 style disclosures.
Framework relevance (framework-level): BRSR, ESRS, IFRS S1, IFRS S2
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS 2 GOV-5 internal control/risk management for sustainability reporting; IFRS S1/S2 governance/control support; BRSR assurance readiness support
What to capture (kernels): Control descriptions per KPI, data lineage/source systems, review & sign-off workflow, change log, internal testing evidence, evidence register
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Controls pack supports ESRS 2 governance disclosures (incl. GOV-4 due diligence and reporting governance). If tracking control metrics (# controls tested, exceptions), keep KPI/control taxonomy stable and maintain comparatives.

Document name: Supplier due diligence pack (if value chain material)
Document description: Supplier segmentation, screening, audits, corrective actions, ESG clauses, and grievance access. Supports S2 and due diligence disclosures.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS S2 value chain disclosures (if material) + ESRS 2 due diligence process; GRI supply chain disclosures; CDP supply chain modules (if used); BRSR value chain disclosures
What to capture (kernels): Supplier list segmentation, screening criteria/workflow, audits/findings, CAPs/closure, ESG clauses, supplier grievance access + metrics
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: ESRS-G1-2 is narrative supplier management disclosure. If tracking quantitative supplier DD metrics (coverage %, audits, CAP closure), maintain segmentation dimensions (tier, geography, risk category) and comparatives year-on-year.

Document description: Stakeholder mapping, engagement plan, engagement records, and evidence of how views influence strategy and materiality.
Framework relevance (framework-level): BRSR, CDP, ESRS, GRI, IFRS S1, TCFD
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS 1 stakeholder inputs to materiality; ESRS 2 SBM stakeholder engagement; GRI stakeholder engagement disclosures; CDP governance/strategy narrative inputs; BRSR stakeholder engagement; TCFD context
What to capture (kernels): Stakeholder map, engagement plan, channels/frequency, logs/themes, how used in materiality and strategy, feedback loop evidence
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Supports materiality evidence trail. If tracking quantitative engagement counts, keep stakeholder-group taxonomy stable and provide year-on-year comparatives (count of engagements, coverage %, key themes frequency).

Document description: Umbrella ESG policy describing governance, topic coverage, KPI architecture, and monitoring cadence; often the top-level mapping anchor across frameworks.
Framework relevance (framework-level): BRSR, CDP, ESRS, GRI, IFRS S1, IFRS S2, TCFD
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS 2 GOV/SBM basis narrative; ESRS MDR policy umbrella; GRI 2 context; IFRS S1 governance/risk; IFRS S2 climate governance (if applicable); CDP governance narratives; BRSR overall approach; TCFD governance pillar
What to capture (kernels): ESG governance model, topic coverage map, KPI selection + definitions, monitoring cadence/escalation, targets register, cross-framework alignment claims, evidence register mapping
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Use these Crossmap DPs for governance/due diligence and supplier management narrative anchors. Any quantitative “inventory” metrics (KPI counts, coverage %) should have stable definitions and year-on-year comparatives.

Document name: ESRS 2 governance documents (ToR, org structure, RACI)
Document description: Board/committee terms of reference and management accountability artifacts for sustainability. Provides evidence for ESRS 2 GOV and oversight disclosures.
Framework relevance (framework-level): BRSR, ESRS, IFRS S1, IFRS S2, TCFD
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS 2 GOV oversight/roles; IFRS S1/S2 governance; BRSR governance disclosures; TCFD governance pillar
What to capture (kernels): Board/committee ToR, oversight roles, org chart/reporting lines, RACI for topic/KPI owners, meeting cadence & materials
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Governance artefacts underpin ESRS 2 GOV disclosures (incl. GOV-4 due diligence). Any quantitative governance metrics (meeting count, attendance %) are optional; if used, keep definitions and comparatives consistent.

Document description: Double materiality methodology, results, and IRO register. Gatekeeper for ESRS topical applicability and a core disclosure subject in ESRS 2/ESRS 1.
Framework relevance (framework-level): BRSR, CDP, ESRS, GRI, IFRS S1, IFRS S2, TCFD
ESRS DP ID(s) (from Crossmap): ESRS-1-PAR-22 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-1-PAR-22-e18d011463114829b37ac95558ad257e?pvs=21), ESRS-1-PAR-24 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-1-PAR-24-918d9b922b854ee0bec7ecef7c37c774?pvs=21), ESRS-1-PAR-25 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-1-PAR-25-a57665df37844af2a6668d58b6d7670d?pvs=21), ESRS-1-PAR-32 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-1-PAR-32-ffd46cd0651d4d829391906054a1c552?pvs=21), ESRS-1-PAR-35 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-1-PAR-35-afb5755b13bb48ef897e6d230a5b1573?pvs=21), ESRS-1-PAR-38 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-1-PAR-38-f3a5d02244d44429878fd13e7f4ab3e2?pvs=21), ESRS-1-PAR-43 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-1-PAR-43-694aef02bfe5439594ebb666ec6d2646?pvs=21), ESRS-1-PAR-44 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-1-PAR-44-dd032aa4525e4b71b4edb46246862761?pvs=21), ESRS-1-PAR-46 (https://www.notion.so/ESRS-1-PAR-46-81c451dbc7fd424995c1ec180724e892?pvs=21)
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS 1 materiality process + ESRS 2 IRO disclosures; IFRS S1/S2 material risks/opportunities; GRI material topics process; CDP risks/opportunities; BRSR material issues narrative; TCFD risks/opportunities governance
What to capture (kernels): Methodology, scoring thresholds, stakeholder inputs, IRO register with horizons, prioritization logic, final material topics + rationale
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Materiality is qualitative in Crossmap. If you keep quantitative scoring outputs, treat them as internal evidence: maintain scoring scale definitions, weighting, stakeholder group splits, and year-on-year comparatives of scores and topic rankings.

Document name: Topic KPI datasets (E, S, G) from source systems
Document description: Primary quantitative datasets and registers (GHG, energy, water, waste, workforce, H&S, pay gap, incidents). Stored in source systems; referenced and controlled for reporting.

Framework relevance (granular): ESRS topical quantitative datapoints (E1–E5, S1–S4, G1); GRI indicators; CDP climate/water/forests modules; IFRS S2 climate metrics; BRSR KPIs; TCFD metrics & targets
What to capture (kernels): Raw KPI tables + definitions, unit/boundary/method, disaggregation, comparatives, restatements, owners/source-of-truth per KPI
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Treat this as the system-of-record pack for the ESRS quantitative DPs linked. Ensure: (1) comparatives where flagged in Crossmap, (2) required disaggregation dimensions from Crossmap are present as columns, (3) calculation standards are documented (e.g., GHG Protocol, GRI/ILO definitions), (4) boundary and restatement log maintained.

Document description: Evidence register, method statements, internal testing, and external validations needed to support third-party assurance over sustainability KPIs and disclosures.
Framework relevance (granular): ESRS statutory assurance preparation (limited assurance baseline); GRI voluntary assurance scope; BRSR KPI assurance readiness
What to capture (kernels): Evidence register per KPI, method statements, version control/change log, internal review/testing, external validations/certificates, assurance scope/provider
Notes on disaggregation/comparative requ: Assurance planning aligns to ESRS 2 governance and due diligence disclosures (GOV-4). Quantitative readiness metrics are optional; if tracked, keep consistent KPI list, evidence status categories, and period-over-period comparatives for completeness %.
